# MCP tool reference

<!-- Generated by `npm run mcp:tools-doc`. Do not edit by hand: this file is
     produced from a live `tools/list` response so it cannot drift. -->

Server `upgradr-mcp-worker` version `0.1.0`, protocol `2025-06-18`, 15 tools.

See [mcp.md](./mcp.md) for authorization, scopes, and how to connect. Every tool below is additionally gated by the `mcp` scope and by row-level security, so a tool only ever sees the calling user's own data.

## Scopes

| Scope | Grants |
|---|---|
| `mcp` | Allows this client to reach your workspace at all. Required. |
| `profile:read` | Your confirmed experience, education, skills, and job search preferences. Unreviewed imports are never shared. |
| `opportunities:read` | Lets the agent see which opportunities you already track so it does not propose the same job twice. |
| `applications:read` | Your opportunities, statuses, follow-ups, notes, and document titles. |
| `applications:write` | Create job proposals in your Inbox, move cards between columns, and add follow-ups and notes. |
| `applications:delete` | Permanently remove items. Every deletion still requires a separate confirmation step. |

## get_candidate_profile

**Get candidate profile**

Return the user's confirmed candidate profile: headline, summary, work experience, education, and skills. Unconfirmed/imported facts are never returned.

Requires scope: `profile:read` (plus `mcp`).

_No arguments._

## get_job_search_preferences

**Get job search preferences**

Return the user's job search preferences: target roles, locations, compensation floor, and exclusions.

Requires scope: `profile:read` (plus `mcp`).

_No arguments._

## search_existing_opportunities

**Search existing opportunities**

Search the user's already-tracked applications by title/company/location/source URL, to check for an existing match before proposing a new one.

Requires scope: `opportunities:read` (plus `mcp`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | no | Match against the job title. Partial matches count. |
| `companyName` | string | no | Match against the company name. Partial matches count. |
| `location` | string | no | Narrow results by location. Only meaningful alongside another filter. |
| `sourceUrl` | string | no | Exact posting URL. The most precise way to check whether a job is already tracked. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Maximum results, 1-50. Defaults to a bounded page. |

## list_known_opportunity_keys

**List known opportunity keys**

Return the de-duplication keys for every opportunity the user already tracks, including closed ones, so an agent can filter its candidates locally before calling create_job_proposals. Each entry carries the canonical source URL, the source provider and its external job id, a normalized company|title|location fingerprint, and the current status. An entry with isClosed true means the user already rejected, withdrew from, dismissed, or archived that opportunity: do not propose it again. Fetch this once per run (paginate with offset, or pass updatedSince to fetch only what changed) rather than searching per candidate.

Requires scope: `opportunities:read` (plus `mcp`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `updatedSince` | string | no | ISO 8601 timestamp. Return only keys for opportunities changed since then, so a repeat run can fetch just the delta. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Keys per page, 1-200. |
| `offset` | integer | no | Number of keys to skip, for paging. |

## get_job_search_dashboard

**Get job search dashboard**

Return an aggregated snapshot of the user's job search: proposal count, active pipeline count, and overdue follow-up count.

Requires scope: `applications:read` (plus `mcp`).

_No arguments._

## search_applications

**Search applications**

Search the user's job applications by status and/or free-text query, paginated.

Requires scope: `applications:read` (plus `mcp`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `proposed` \| `shortlisted` \| `saved` \| `preparing` \| `applied` \| `screening` \| `interviewing` \| `offer` \| `accepted` \| `rejected` \| `withdrawn` \| `dismissed` \| `archived` | no | Restrict to one pipeline status. Omit to search across all of them. |
| `query` | string | no | Free-text search over title, company, and location. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Results per page, 1-50. |
| `offset` | integer | no | Number of results to skip, for paging. |

## get_application

**Get application**

Return a single job application by id.

Requires scope: `applications:read` (plus `mcp`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `applicationId` | string | yes | Id of the opportunity, as returned by search_applications. |

## create_job_proposals

**Create job proposals**

Propose up to 20 new job opportunities for the user to review. Each proposal must cite a valid HTTP(S) source URL. Duplicates are detected server-side against every opportunity the user owns, including ones they already closed, so no proposal is ever silently duplicated: each item comes back as created, duplicate (same provider job id or same canonical source URL), or possible_duplicate (same company, title and location found at a different URL). Duplicate results include the existing opportunity's id and current status, so a closed match means the user already rejected or dismissed that job — do not propose it again. Set allowSimilar on an item only to override a possible_duplicate you have confirmed is a genuinely different opening. Use list_known_opportunity_keys once per run to filter candidates before calling this tool.

Requires scope: `applications:write` (plus `mcp`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `proposals` | array of object | yes | Between 1 and 20 proposals, each evaluated independently. |
| `proposals[].title` | string | yes | Job title exactly as published, e.g. 'Senior iOS Engineer'. |
| `proposals[].companyName` | string | yes | Hiring company name. Used for duplicate detection, so keep it consistent. |
| `proposals[].location` | string | no | Work location as published, e.g. 'Stockholm, Sweden' or 'Remote (EU)'. |
| `proposals[].sourceUrl` | string | yes | Canonical HTTP(S) URL of the posting. Required, and the strongest duplicate key. |
| `proposals[].sourceProvider` | string | yes | Where it was found, e.g. 'linkedin', 'greenhouse', 'company-site'. |
| `proposals[].externalId` | string | no | The provider's own stable job id, when the posting exposes one. Supply it whenever available: combined with sourceProvider it is the most reliable duplicate key, and it survives URL changes. |
| `proposals[].description` | string | no | Job description text. Stored verbatim for the user to read. |
| `proposals[].compensationMin` | number | no | Bottom of the published salary range, as an annual figure. |
| `proposals[].compensationMax` | number | no | Top of the published salary range, as an annual figure. |
| `proposals[].compensationCurrency` | string | no | ISO 4217 currency code for the compensation range, e.g. 'SEK', 'EUR'. |
| `proposals[].matchScore` | integer | no | Your assessment of fit against the user's profile, 0-100. |
| `proposals[].matchRationale` | string | no | Short explanation of the score, shown to the user alongside the proposal. |
| `proposals[].strengths` | array of string | no | Concrete reasons the user fits this role. |
| `proposals[].gaps` | array of string | no | Requirements the user does not clearly meet. Be honest; this is decision support. |
| `proposals[].confidence` | number | no | How confident you are in the extracted facts themselves, 0-1. |
| `proposals[].allowSimilar` | boolean | no | Override a possible_duplicate result for this item only, when you have confirmed it is a genuinely different opening. Exact source-URL and provider job-id duplicates can never be overridden. |

## move_application_status

**Move application status**

Transition a job application to a new status in its pipeline.

Requires scope: `applications:write` (plus `mcp`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `applicationId` | string | yes | Id of the opportunity to transition. |
| `newStatus` | `proposed` \| `shortlisted` \| `saved` \| `preparing` \| `applied` \| `screening` \| `interviewing` \| `offer` \| `accepted` \| `rejected` \| `withdrawn` \| `dismissed` \| `archived` | yes | Target status. The transition is recorded in the opportunity's status history. |
| `note` | string | no | Why the status changed. Shown to the user on the activity timeline. |

## list_follow_ups

**List follow-ups**

List the user's follow-up tasks, optionally scoped to one application, ordered by due date.

Requires scope: `applications:read` (plus `mcp`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `applicationId` | string | no | Only follow-ups for this opportunity. Omit for all of them. |
| `includeCompleted` | boolean | no | Include already-completed follow-ups. Defaults to false. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Results per page, 1-50. |
| `offset` | integer | no | Number of results to skip, for paging. |

## create_follow_up

**Create follow-up**

Create a follow-up task for a job application.

Requires scope: `applications:write` (plus `mcp`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `applicationId` | string | yes | Opportunity this follow-up belongs to. |
| `title` | string | yes | What needs doing, e.g. 'Send thank-you note to recruiter'. |
| `notes` | string | no | Extra context for the user. |
| `dueAt` | string | no | ISO 8601 due date. Past dates count as overdue immediately. |

## complete_follow_up

**Complete follow-up**

Mark a follow-up task as complete.

Requires scope: `applications:write` (plus `mcp`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `followUpId` | string | yes | Id of the follow-up, as returned by list_follow_ups. |

## add_note

**Add note**

Add a note to a job application, recorded as agent-authored with source provenance.

Requires scope: `applications:write` (plus `mcp`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `applicationId` | string | yes | Opportunity to attach the note to. |
| `body` | string | yes | Note text. Stored as agent-authored, with your client identity recorded alongside it. |

## prepare_destructive_operation

**Prepare destructive operation**

Request a single-use confirmation token for a destructive action (e.g. deleting an application, follow-up, or note, or archiving a batch of applications). The action does not happen until confirm_operation is called with the returned token, and the token expires after 15 minutes.

Requires scope: `applications:delete` (plus `mcp`).

One of the following shapes:

**operationType: `delete_application`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operationType` | `delete_application` | yes |  |
| `applicationId` | string | yes | Opportunity to delete, along with its notes, follow-ups, and history. |
| `reason` | string | no | Why this is being deleted. Shown to the user in the confirmation summary and kept in the audit trail. |

**operationType: `delete_follow_up`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operationType` | `delete_follow_up` | yes |  |
| `followUpId` | string | yes | Follow-up task to delete. |
| `reason` | string | no | Why this is being deleted. Shown to the user in the confirmation summary and kept in the audit trail. |

**operationType: `delete_note`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operationType` | `delete_note` | yes |  |
| `noteId` | string | yes | Note to delete. |
| `reason` | string | no | Why this is being deleted. Shown to the user in the confirmation summary and kept in the audit trail. |

**operationType: `bulk_archive_applications`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operationType` | `bulk_archive_applications` | yes |  |
| `applicationIds` | array of string | yes | Between 1 and 20 opportunities to archive in a single confirmed operation. |
| `reason` | string | no | Why this is being deleted. Shown to the user in the confirmation summary and kept in the audit trail. |

## confirm_operation

**Confirm operation**

Execute a previously prepared destructive operation using its single-use confirmation token from prepare_destructive_operation.

Requires scope: `applications:delete` (plus `mcp`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operationToken` | string | yes | The single-use token returned by prepare_destructive_operation. Valid for 15 minutes, and only for the exact operation that was summarized. |

## Calling a tool

```sh
curl -sS "$UPGRADR_MCP_URL" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $UPGRADR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -H "accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_job_search_dashboard","arguments":{}}}'
```

Get `$UPGRADR_ACCESS_TOKEN` from `npm run mcp:login -- --email you@example.com`.
